item.title: Chance the Rapper Performs Stirring Muhammad Ali Tribute ‘I Was a Rock’ at Gordon Parks Foundation Annual Awards
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to this week's edition of 'Trending on Billboard'. I'm your host, and today we're talking about a star-studded night in NYC. The Gordon Parks Foundation held its 20th-anniversary awards dinner and auction, and it was a night to remember. Let's dive in."
[Soft music transitions in]
Host: "Chance the Rapper took the stage at Cipriani 42nd Street, performing a stirring tribute to Muhammad Ali with his song 'I Was a Rock'. He was joined by the Anthony Morgan's Inspirational Choir of Harlem, and even included audio from a 1977 Ali interview. This isn't the first time Chance has paid tribute to the boxing legend - he also performed 'I Was a Rock' at the 2016 ESPY Awards."
[Short music break]
Host: "The night was all about celebrating the legacy of Gordon Parks, a legendary photographer and civil rights activist. Parks was a pioneer in narrating the Black experience in America through his photography, and his work continues to inspire artists and activists today. Chance himself said it's humbling to be recognized in a space honoring Parks and Ali, and that his goal is to tell the truth through his work, just like they did."
[Music transitions to a slightly upbeat tone]
Host: "The evening brought together some big names in music, social justice, and philanthropy. Alicia Keys and Swizz Beatz were co-chairs for the night, while Colin Kaepernick presented an award. John Legend was one of the honorees, and Pharrell welcomed him to the stage. The night raised an impressive $3 million for the Gordon Parks Foundation, which supports educational and artistic initiatives, as well as fellowships and scholarships for emerging artists and writers."
[Outro music plays]
Host: "That's all for today's episode. The Gordon Parks Foundation is doing amazing work, and it's great to see artists and activists coming together to celebrate his legacy. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next episode of 'Trending on Billboard'."
